issues.legal_issue: A protected member of a joint family is not entitled to postponement of a tenant’s statutory purchase when the member’s separated share in the land is not proportionate to that member’s share in the joint family property.
material_facts: The land was held by a joint family and was in the possession of tenants who were deemed to have purchased it under the statutory scheme.
A minor family member claimed the protection available to a landlord in a protected category after the family partitioned the land and allotted him a share.
The minor’s mother was entitled to a share in the land but received none; the share allotted to the minor was therefore not proportionate to his share in the entire joint family property.
The final fact-finding authority found that the allotted share was not proportionate having regard to the area, assessment, classification and value of the land.
issues.conclusion: The family partition did not qualify the minor for the statutory postponement of the tenants’ purchase, so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 32F(1)(a) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, the protected-landlord postponement does not apply where the protected person belongs to a joint family that includes a member outside the protected categories, unless the protected person’s share is separated by metes and bounds and is proportionate to that person’s share in the entire joint family property, assessed with regard to the area, assessment, classification and value of the land. Section 32 provides for the tenant’s purchase. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: tenant_statutory_purchase_proceeding and protected_landlord_is_joint_family_member and joint_family_has_unprotected_member and share_separated_from_family and not land_share_is_proportionate_to_family_share

predicates.tenant_statutory_purchase_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s statutory purchase of agricultural land and a landlord’s claim to postpone that purchase.
predicates.protected_landlord_is_joint_family_membe: The landlord claiming protection belongs to a joint family and is within a category for which the purchase may be postponed.
predicates.joint_family_has_unprotected_member: At least one member of the joint family is outside the categories eligible for that protection.
predicates.share_separated_from_family: The protected family member’s share in the land has been separated from the joint family property.
predicates.land_share_is_proportionate_to_family_sh: The land allotted to the protected family member is proportionate to that member’s share in the entire joint family property, having regard to the relevant characteristics of the land.

issues.definition: When a protected family member claims postponement in a tenant’s statutory purchase proceeding, the postponement is unavailable if the joint family has an unprotected member, the protected member’s share has been separated, and that land share is not proportionate to the member’s share in the family property.
